chapter: Harlem musicians and the road with Armstrong
title: Paying for uniforms and arguing with Glaser
summary: Uniforms were deducted from pay, so Holmes told Glaser he would wear his own paid-for suit wherever he liked.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Now, when you first went in a band in those days, you got fitted for uniforms right away. How did that work? You went to a tailor or something?

Yeah. Well, the tailor would make the uniforms, you know. He made all the uniforms. He was a... In fact, the tailor practically made his living off of Louis Armstrong's band and Joe Glaser...because there was a lot of bands. Joe had a lot of irons in the fire, you know. And this tailor practically made his living off it.
Because some bands had like three and four changes.
Oh, we had a lot of uniforms. We had a lot of uniforms. But they was all suits; they was suits we could wear.
But we had to pay for them.
Yeah, we had to pay for them.
So that was deducted from your salary?
So that they made sure they got the money.
Yeah. Yeah. Yeah, we used to pay for

them. They weren't buying them. They should have been paying for them. One time, Joe Glaser and I, we had a little argument about the uniforms, you know. We weren't supposed to wear the uniforms in the street, naturally enough...but it wasn't nothin' but a suit.

So here we are, we're down in one of them Southern towns one Sunday morning and gettin' ready to leave. So I come to the bus all dressed up in my uniform. And Joe Glaser saw me about a block away, and he hollered at me. Joe hollered anyway; he got excited, you know, he would holler anyway. He says, "Charlie, you know you're not supposed to wear that uniform out in the street!" I said, "Well, Mr. Glaser, if you don't want me to wear a uniform in the street, you pay for it." I said, "I paid for this one. I wear this anywhere I please. You don't tell me where to wear this. This is mine." Case closed. He said no more. I was perfectly right. You can't tell me where to wear my clothes. If he wants me not to wear his uniform in the street, let him pay for it, and I'll wear it wherever he says.
